Messages.Author: Neil
Messages.Body:
Omael <omael....@gmail.com> wrote in message
news:1149716782.5...@g10g2000cwb.googlegroups.com...


I had the experience of first being the guy who was complaining about imbued
when they were new and I didn't know any of the rules or the new cards or
types of cards. It just seemed like the imbued player was just piling up
cards and I had no idea what he was doing without doing a lot of reading and
remembering.

Then I actually bought most of his imbued cards off him cause he wasn't that
interested in them any more and then I had the reverse experience of being
the guy who was enjoying playing his deck but everyone was yawning and
barely interested in what I was doing.

I realized a few things would help:

1. Introduce the set to new people with a brief introduction, explaining the
rules simply in your own words -- don't just give them the rules cards. For
instance, a new person's mind might boggle when he sees how the conviction
cards pile up on your minions. Just explain that there's only three kinds of
conviction cards, and show them to him ahead of time.

2. Once you've gotten the hang of playing with them, try to make sure your
deck is focused on going forward, and not just on piling up a bunch of cards
that you'll never use. Part of the problem too, is that a lot of imbued
cards have multiple uses, which means that even after reading all your
cards, opponents may still not know what to expect, or remember what
everything does. Maybe instead of starting out with an all-imbued deck
against new players, make a deck that only use a little of the new stuff.

3. The new mechanics might make your turn drag if you don't know what you
are doing. Take your turns quickly as you are more accustomed to the cards.
Have your conviction cards ready to play at the beginning of your turn, and
know which ones you are going to play. I made the mistake of putting all my
discards in a plastic card box and then I was digging through it every turn
which was, I'm sure, very annoying.

4. If you use cards that hurt everyone on the table, be they Smiling Jack or
Gehenna cards you have to expect some table hate, and you probably deserve
some of it. If people can play their deck a lot easier if you are simply
gone, then they may well enjoy watching you be ousted. How about using some
cards that can help out your cross-table allies (like Owain Evans for
example) so that they actually want you to stay in the game?

5. Make sure you know all the rules, because you may be the only one paying
attention to your deck. Particularly remember to burn convictions when
necessary as a cost -- I found the indication to do that on some cards to
not be as clear as it could be. Play everything the right way and soon
everyone will know what's going to happen. After a few games with the
imbued, hopefully the other players will realize that they don't always have
to be annoying (any more than any other deck). Remember that people fear
most what they don't understand!

6. I do kind of appreciate how the natural instinct of vampire players is
to destroy the hunters. If all else fails, just enjoy being a pariah and
pack your deck with plenty of stuff to make people regret they messed with
you! Any deck that is uberpowerful will get crosstable hate and so you have
to be able to deal with it.

Hope it helps. Thanks for the oportunity to write down some ideas that have
been on my mind.

Neil

> Everyone that have played imbued knows what i mean, so what did you do

> I mean, it's ok to play with that in a tournament, but in casual play

See, I think currently everyone is still traumatized by the standard
"sucks to be a vampire" decks that most Imbued decks tend to be (ya
know, all the horrible events, Millicent Smith, whatever)--these decks
tend to not only be wildly disruptive to everyone, but they also slow
the game down a billion times, as everyone needs to read a hundred
cards on the table every time they take an action. This sort of thing
makes everyone mad, and results in the whole table conspring to kill
the Imbued deck just to get them off the table.

The long term solution? Everyone needs to develop non disruptive Imbued
deck strategies. Ya know, ones that don't revolve around horrible
Gehenna events and the master cards that make everyone hate you.
Eventually, when people have Imbued technology that doesn't result in
everyone hating them, people will stop hating them.

-Peter

Messages.Author: Fred Scott
Messages.Body:
"Omael" <omael....@gmail.com> wrote in message
news:1149716782.5...@g10g2000cwb.googlegroups.com...

> Everyone that have played imbued knows what i mean, so what did you do
> to avoid crosstables rushes and/or bleeds? what about crosstable
> ancient influence?
> I mean, it's ok to play with that in a tournament, but in casual play
> it just pisses the player without a good reason.

Table hate is a legitimate response to a real metagame problem Imbued
decks cause for current non-Imbued archetypes. In some respects, its
an unfortunate game design problem to make the entire metagame shift
so abruptly to a new expansion. But if a metagame shift will fix the
problem, eventually peoples' decks will change and the problem will
go away on its own. I say "if" because I suspect that if shifting
how non-Imbued decks to cope with Imbued decks weakens the former too
much when not playing Imbued decks, this will cause a quirky metagame
issue that will just result in a greater influence of luck on game
outcomes (e.g. who has an Imbued as his prey, meaning that he's
either screwed if he doesn't get effective help from table hate or
charmed if he does because he gets an easy victory point).

If the metagame can't shift enough, there's always hope that the
designers will eventually bridge the gap by printing more convenient,
usable anti-Imbued cards similar to Break the Code. We'll see...

Fred

Don't do that. Just hang onto the Slow Withering until it's a good time
to play it. Most of the time it'll count against your hand size while in
play, so there's not much disadvantage to not playing it for a while. Let

to you.

Messages.Author: Ector
Messages.Body:

Looks like you've got a very strange players :) Our players really like
to see new things and new mechanics, though the majority isn't ready to
USE them.
Talking about the table hate, just ask yourself: is it well-deserved or
not? If your deck actively messes with everyone's game, it may be. Good
decks kill their preys, slow their predators and HELP their allies. You
can do these things even with Imbued.
For instance, your Anna "Dictatrix11" Suljic can provide 2 blood to an
ally's vampire - why not include her or at least a bunch of Rejuvenates
if you plan to drain the vampires' blood with Gehenna cards?
Ancient Influence usually isn't a "crosstable hate" - somebody wants to
get pool with it. Again, you can prepare to this threat - personally I
prefer adding one support vampire to an Imbued deck (see my !Malk
newsletters for details). Add Marie Faucigny - and voila! Ancient
Influence will give you 2 pool instead of taking 5 away.
Finally, you should know your cards very well and be able to explain
their mechanics to any player. Imbued aren't overpowered, and
crosstable actions against them are just silly - every sentient player
should understand this if you care to explain.
If all else fails, you can find a friend willing to play Imbued, build
two Imbued decks to avoid contest, and play "table hate" yourself :)
This should FORCE your players to get accustomed to the Imbued and
understand their mechanics, and you will be able to play normally
afterwards.
Good luck!

Yours,
Ector

There are two possibilities.

1st. Your deck is really very strong, so ganging on you is the only way
to stop you. Then the reaction is not different to the reaction to some
Weenie or Arika decks. The only thing you can do, make a deck that is
not so obviously strong. Using fewer Gehenna events for example.

2nd. The crosstable play against your deck is bad play. People dont
like your deck, and by not playing to win play against you. That really
is a problem with playing style. On the long run, it would be necessary
to teach your players how to play to win. What can you do now? Show the
players, that it is bad to play crosstable without a reason. If they
all try to kill you, sell your soul. Make a table splitting deal with
your prey to get one VP. If you are successful, tell all that you
needed to make such a dirty deal, because it was the only thing you
could do, after they all attacked you.

Messages.Author: pd...@lightlink.com
Messages.Body:
LSJ wrote:
> The easiest way to avoid table hate is to avoid giving the table a
> reason to hate you.

Precisely. My current Imbued deck is totally hateable. It plays with
all the horrible Gehenna events. And Millicent Smith. And all that
other annoying as hell crap. And everyone hates it. So I swore I'd take
it apart and make something new, so everyone would stop hating me :-)

The current state of affairs has, for the most part, the Imbued being
used for tier one technology--the "sucks to be a vampire" deck, as that
is the most obvious strategy to use the Imbued in. Which is good for
the Imbued, but bad for everyone else, so they tend to get whacked
cross table just so they can be ousted at which point everyone else
gets to play a normal game (kind of similar to Nergal, the "Let's all
kill Nergal, and then play a regular game of VTES..." factor).

When everyone figures out tier two+ technology (i.e. Imbued decks that
aren't likely to generate unreasonable table hate), this will all go
away I'm sure, as there will no longer be incentive to cross table oust
them (currently, there is often very strong incentive to cross table
oust the Imbued--the want to be able to play a card without having to
read 5 events and to 3 random things just to play it).

-Peter

Messages.Author: FC
Messages.Body:
Ector wrote:

> Talking about the table hate, just ask yourself: is it well-deserved or
> not? If your deck actively messes with everyone's game, it may be. Good
> decks kill their preys, slow their predators and HELP their allies. You
> can do these things even with Imbued.

Yes. Good point.

> For instance, your Anna "Dictatrix11" Suljic can provide 2 blood to an
> ally's vampire - why not include her or at least a bunch of Rejuvenates
> if you plan to drain the vampires' blood with Gehenna cards?
> Ancient Influence usually isn't a "crosstable hate" - somebody wants to
> get pool with it. Again, you can prepare to this threat - personally I
> prefer adding one support vampire to an Imbued deck (see my !Malk
> newsletters for details). Add Marie Faucigny - and voila! Ancient
> Influence will give you 2 pool instead of taking 5 away.

Well. there is advantages to being all imbued. You vampire support with
be a glaring target for Fame, Taste of Vitae, Anathemas, War Ghoul
rushes and any other of the many, many popular cards that requires a
vampire target.

On the other hand with a vampire you can take actions to get the Rack,
remove smiling jack, rescue or diabolize vampires and any of the other
the many, many situations where you need an vampire.

I would think all imbued are the stronger choice in most cases.

> Finally, you should know your cards very well and be able to explain
> their mechanics to any player. Imbued aren't overpowered, and
> crosstable actions against them are just silly - every sentient player
> should understand this if you care to explain.

They seem powerful. Quite powerful.

> If all else fails, you can find a friend willing to play Imbued, build
> two Imbued decks to avoid contest, and play "table hate" yourself :)
> This should FORCE your players to get accustomed to the Imbued and
> understand their mechanics, and you will be able to play normally
> afterwards.
> Good luck!
>

I don't like the idea of forcing anyone to doing anything. If anyone
tells me to please not use an imbued deck i will accomodate them, I have
some decks to choose from and see no need to aggravate people who are
spending their free time to enjoy a game with me.

In our group we have seen the "screw vampires" deck and it received a
chilly welcome.

Sure we taunt breeder, weenie, S&B and basically any kind of deck that
does not involve ripping someones head off but thats the a gleam in the
eye. When Wyrmwood hits that gleam is gone.

Its all very well to know that such decks can be made but in the end we
all seem to be trying to "soften the impact" so to speak - with just a
few events, with a support vampire or whatever and i must say Imbued
seem very competive without all the hate stuff. My only imbued deck got
2 GW in its three first games and i made many rookie mistakes with them.

Frede
